title: Part IV
author: David Hume
summary: Cleanthes says that those who call God's nature incomprehensible are no better than atheists. Philo replies that a divine mind full of ordered ideas needs explaining just as much as an ordered world, so explaining one by the other begins an endless regress.

notes.on: the Indian philosopher and his elephant
notes.note: The Indian holds that the world rests on an elephant and the elephant on a tortoise, but cannot say what the tortoise rests on. Locke tells the story in the *Essay concerning Human Understanding*, ii. 13. 19 and ii. 23. 2.
